description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy across three different measures—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.86 to 1.00. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is scaled linearly with a range from 0.86 to 1.00, marked at intervals of 0.02. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines at 0.2 intervals. The "Final Accuracy" is represented by a solid blue line with square markers, which remains relatively stable around a value of 0.95, showing slight fluctuations but maintaining a high level of accuracy across all initial confidence levels. The "Δ Accuracy," depicted by a dashed orange line with diamond markers, starts at approximately 0.35 when initial confidence is 0.86, decreases to a minimum of about 0.02 near an initial confidence of 0.95, and then increases again to around 0.28 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The "Initial Accuracy" is shown by a dotted green line with circular markers, beginning at approximately 0.65 when initial confidence is 0.86, increasing to a peak of about 0.92 near an initial confidence of 0.96, and then decreasing slightly to around 0.78 at an initial confidence of 1.00. Error bars are present for each data point, indicating variability in the measurements.
